paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates how the metric labeled “minADE\(_{20}\) (←)” varies with the number of in-context examples for two methods (“ST-ES” and “Random”). The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0 to 8 with tick labels shown at regular intervals of 2 (0, 2, 4, 6, 8). The y-axis is labeled “minADE\(_{20}\) (←),” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from about 15.1 up to 18.0, with labeled ticks at 0.5 increments (15.5, 16.0, 16.5, 17.0, 17.5, 18.0). The ST-ES series is drawn as a solid blue line with circular markers; it starts near 17.0 at 0 examples, drops to about 15.4 at 1 example, then stays close to ~15.2 from 2 through 8 examples with small fluctuations (around 15.22 at 2, ~15.20 at 3, ~15.22 at 4, ~15.18 at 5–6, and ending near ~15.25 at 8). The Random series is drawn as a solid orange line with circular markers; it begins near 17.95 at 0 examples, decreases to about 17.33 at 1 and ~17.12 at 2, reaches around ~17.01 at 3 and ~16.93 at 4, then remains near ~16.95 from 5 through 7 and ends slightly lower near ~16.89 at 8 examples.
